messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: potential cross-tenant read detected for customer 'garnet' (VPC vpc-101) on dedicated pool dp-7. Alert score: 87. Snapshot: multiple KV reads returned keys prefixed with another tenant ID. Please acknowledge if on-call.

oncall-alex: acked — I'm on it. Paging SRE rotation. Setting priority HIGH.

eng-sre-maya: can someone paste the alert details? I only have the short stream.

incident-bot: Alert details:
- time_window: 2026-03-15T02:32:00Z to 2026-03-15T02:34:00Z
- node_ids: gpu-node-17, gpu-node-18
- symptom: kv-read responses included keys with prefix tenant-id: 642 instead of 431
- sample_keys: ["431:session:ab12", "642:user:zz99"]
- initial_detector: cache-prefix-guard-v2

eng-platform-ryan: I pulled the logs for dp-7. I see a routing update at 02:31:58 that touched kube-svc routing table — looks like a rollout of a new proxy config. Rolling back now?

oncall-alex: Ryan, do we have evidence that the rollout touched tenant prefix translation? If so, isolate.

eng-platform-ryan: There's a config change to envoy sidecar that loosened prefix validation (changed allow_list regex). I'm running a rollback to the previous config sha (sha: 9f3b2a). Command: `kubectl -n dedicated apply -f envoy-config-rollback.yaml`

infra-elly: I've initiated a graceful drain of gpu-node-18 and evicted all dp-7 pods from that host to stop further reads. Eviction command: `kubectl drain gpu-node-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sre-luis: Running a manual KV probe against dp-7 from a sandbox: `curl -X POST https://dp-7.internal/kv/query -d '{"key":"431:session:ab12"}'` — initial attempt returned a 200 with payload containing fields that reference tenant 642. Captured payload in logs.

cust-eng-julie: Confirming customer report: Garnet reported a small set of unexpected user IDs appearing in response for a customer-only audit. They asked us to escalate. We told them we're investigating and will follow up within 30m.

eng-sre-maya: Ok we have two correlated actions: 1) rollback envoy config; 2) isolate affected node/pool. After rollback, check if subsequent KV reads still surface cross-tenant keys. Ryan/Luis, can you re-run the probe after rollback?

eng-platform-ryan: Rollback applied to the control plane at 02:36:05Z. New pod rollout in progress.

sre-luis: Re-probing at 02:37:12Z. `curl` now returns expected tenant-scoped keys only. No cross-tenant prefixes in the sample set. Captured diff of responses stored in s3://redwood-incident-evidence/garnet/3255550000/response-diff.log

oncall-alex: Good. That suggests config change caused the symptom. Preserve evidence and start a formal mitigation timeline.

eng-sre-maya: Immediate mitigation summary to paste to customer: "We observed an unintended routing regression caused by a recent proxy config change in a dedicated pool. We rolled back the change and isolated the affected host. Our probes after rollback show no further cross-tenant reads. We are preserving logs and continuing forensic analysis. No confirmed unauthorised data exfiltration beyond the initial sample set; we will follow up with a full scope within 4 hours." Thoughts? :lock: :page_with_curl:

cust-eng-julie: That's fine to send. Add that we will open a dedicated support escalation channel and provide a redacted artifact sample. Also mention we're rotating any keys that could be impacted if we detect PII.

eng-platform-ryan: I'll open a support case and generate redacted sample. Case: RED-INC-20260315-431-GARNET. Link: https://console.redwood/support/RED-INC-20260315-431-GARNET

infra-elly: Forensic checklist I'm running:
```
- snapshot node (gpu-node-18) disk state
- collect envoy configs for last 24h
- collect kube events for dp-7
- preserve in immutable storage path s3://redwood-incident-evidence/garnet/3255550000/
```

eng-sre-maya: Add runbook refs: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/tenant_isolation and https://docs.redwood/incident/playbooks/kv_crossread. Also add postmortem owner: maya (SRE).

sre-luis: Quick note — metrics show a tiny spike in KV read latency coincident with the config rollout (02:31:40Z). I suspect the loose regex allowed a misrouted prefix to bypass the guard. Will run a unit test on the validator next.

oncall-alex: Assignments:
- maya: lead postmortem + customer follow-up (4h scope)
- ryan: rollback timeline + config diff (immediate)
- luis: reproduce test + evidence capture (immediate)
- elly: forensic snapshots + immutable storage (immediate)
- julie: customer comms + escalation channel (immediate)

cust-eng-julie: Customer is asking for ETA on final confirmation. I'll tell them we'll have a 4h scope and a 24h detailed report.

eng-platform-ryan: Config diff (relevant lines):
```diff
- prefix_validation: 
-   allow: ".*"
+ prefix_validation:
+   allow: "^tenant-[0-9]+:"
```
Rollback re-applied the stricter anchor.

eng-sre-maya: Noted. Action: enforce linting on proxy config PRs and add a unit test that verifies prefix_validation enforce anchors. I'll create a follow-up JIRA: RED-5432.

sre-luis: When we rotate keys, we should confirm cache invalidation across dp-7. Otherwise old tokens may linger in KV caches. Plan: after key rotation, run cache flush on dp-7 and verify with probe.

infra-elly: Flushing caches requires a draining window. I'll coordinate a minimal window and post timing here. Tentatively scheduling cache flush 03:15Z (low traffic).

oncall-alex: Customer comms draft (julie, please edit):
"Hi Garnet — we detected a routing regression in a dedicated pool which may have returned limited keys from another tenant during a brief window. We rolled back the change and isolated the host. At this time we have no evidence of broad data exposure. We are preserving artifacts and will provide a full scope within 4 hours and a detailed report in 24 hours. If you prefer immediate offboarding to a fresh dedicated pool, we can arrange that. — Redwood Incident Response"

cust-eng-julie: Sent that wording to the customer at 02:50Z. They acknowledged and requested the redacted sample.

eng-sre-maya: Logging follow-ups:
- collect list of all keys returned in the sample (done)
- redact PII and upload to secure case (ryan)
- postmortem timeline draft (maya)

sre-luis: Reproduction notes: failed test case where envoy regex `.*` allowed an unexpected header `x-tenant-prefix` to be forwarded and interpreted by prefix-mapper. PR to fix test: https://git.redwood/prefix-mapper/pulls/112

infra-elly: Node snapshot completed at 03:05Z and uploaded to s3://redwood-incident-evidence/garnet/3255550000/node-snapshots/gpu-node-18.img.gz

eng-platform-ryan: Redacted sample uploaded to secure case. Also added hash: sha256: d2f2...ab9.

eng-sre-maya: Closing immediate mitigation steps here: rollback complete, affected node drained, probes clean, customer notified, evidence preserved. Remaining tasks moved to the incident ticket RED-5432 and will be tracked there.

oncall-alex: Closing pager. If anything new surfaces, re-open here. Great coordination everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed (severity reduced to S2). Auto-generated follow-up checklist assigned.

eng-sre-maya: Postmortem owner will post a first-draft timeline in the incident ticket within 6 hours. I'll include remediation actions: stricter config PR validation, unit tests for prefix parsing, and automated rollout gating for proxy changes that touch prefix_validation.

cust-eng-julie: Customer asked about a timeline for possible dedicated pool offboarding. I'll coordinate with sales/solutions to estimate days for reprovisioning and data migration.

sre-luis: Note for postmortem: consider adding an active assertion in the runtime that rejects keys not matching tenant_id context before returning KV results — defensive check.

eng-platform-ryan: Will open PR to add a CI check that runs a small set of negative tests against config changes (RED-5433).

eng-sre-maya: Thanks team. End of thread."
